knownFor.label: Constitution of India
knownFor.note: The world’s longest written national constitution.

knownFor.label: Space programme (Chandrayaan)
knownFor.note: Landed near the Moon’s south pole in 2023.

knownFor.label: Khadi
knownFor.note: Hand-spun cloth, a symbol of the independence movement.

location.value: South Asia: 28 states and 8 union territories. Capital New Delhi. Area about 3.29 million km².

terrain.value: The Himalayas, the Indo-Gangetic plain, the Deccan plateau, deserts and long coastlines.

climate.value: Monsoon-dependent, and vulnerable to droughts, floods, cyclones and heatwaves.

resources.value: Farmland, coal, iron ore, and a large labour force.

disasters.value: The Bhopal gas disaster (1984). The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. Frequent floods and cyclones.

population.value: 1,210,854,977 in the 2011 census, and about 1.48 billion estimated in 2026, the world’s most populous country.

urbanisation.value: Rapid urbanisation. Megacities include Mumbai, Delhi and Kolkata.

disease.value: Major public-health campaigns (polio eliminated by 2014). COVID-19 caused a severe wave in 2021.

migration.value: Partition (1947) displaced 12–20 million people. There is a large worldwide Indian diaspora.

economicBase.value: Services, industry and agriculture. Economic liberalisation since 1991.

tradeRoutes.value: IT and service exports, pharmaceuticals, and trade with the US, China, the EU and the Gulf.

wealth.value: GDP about $4.06 trillion nominal and $19.19 trillion PPP (3rd largest) in 2026 estimates. Income per person remains lower-middle.

moneyAndTax.value: The Indian rupee. The 1991 balance-of-payments crisis led to liberalisation.

inequality.value: Gini 25.5 (2022). HDI 0.685 (2023). Large rural poverty has been reduced in recent decades.

governmentType.value: A federal parliamentary democratic republic since the constitution came into force (26 January 1950): the world’s largest democracy.

keyRulers.value: Jawaharlal Nehru (1947–1964). Indira Gandhi. Rajiv Gandhi. Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Manmohan Singh. Narendra Modi (since 2014).

succession.value: Regular elections to the Lok Sabha (543 seats). The prime minister leads the majority.

institutions.value: The Constitution (1950), an independent Election Commission, the Supreme Court, and federal states.

stability.value: The Emergency (1975–77), when civil liberties were suspended. Insurgencies and conflicts in Kashmir and the Northeast.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalry between national parties (Congress, BJP) and regional parties.

armyAndTech.value: One of the world’s largest militaries, and nuclear-armed since 1974/1998.

majorWars.value: Wars with Pakistan (1947, 1965, 1971 – Bangladesh’s independence – and Kargil 1999). The 1962 Sino-Indian border war. The Galwan Valley clash (2020).

territoryChange.value: Integrated the princely states (1947–49), Goa (1961) and Sikkim (1975). Kashmir is disputed between India, Pakistan and China.

alliancesRivals.value: A founder of the Non-Aligned Movement. Rivals: Pakistan and China. A growing partnership with the US.

inventions.value: The Green Revolution in farming (1960s), a space programme (Chandrayaan, Mars Orbiter), and IT services.

scienceEducation.value: The IITs and a large university system. Literacy has risen substantially since independence.

openness.value: An inward-looking planned economy until 1991, then opening to trade and investment.

communicationTransport.value: Indian Railways (one of the world’s largest networks), highways, air travel, and cheap mobile internet since 2016.

religion.value: Hinduism 79.8%, Islam 14.2% (2011 census), plus Christianity, Sikhism, Buddhism and Jainism. Officially a secular state.

languageWriting.value: Hindi and English for central government. 22 scheduled languages and hundreds more.

artsArchitecture.value: Bollywood and regional cinema, classical music and dance, literature, and ancient monuments.

socialStructure.value: Caste persists in society despite constitutional bans on discrimination and reservations (affirmative action) for disadvantaged groups.

sharedIdentity.value: “Unity in diversity”: a pluralist national identity. Motto: “Satyameva Jayate” (Truth alone triumphs).

dailyLife.value: Village houses and city apartments; rice, roti, dal and vegetables; family life often in joint families.

neighbours.value: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.

ideasReligions.value: Gandhian non-violence influenced civil-rights movements worldwide.

colonisation.value: Colonised by Britain (East India Company rule, then the British Raj 1858–1947). Independent on 15 August 1947 with Partition.

riseSignals.value: Independence (1947), a durable democratic constitution, the Green Revolution, and economic reforms since 1991.

peakPeriod.value: Ongoing: rapid growth since the 1990s, making it one of the world’s largest economies.

declineSignals.value: Not in decline. Challenges named in the sources include poverty, inequality, communal tensions, and border disputes.

outcome.value: Ongoing: a federal parliamentary republic and the world’s most populous country.

sources.value: Census data, official statistics and modern histories. Checked against Wikipedia (“India”) on 6 Nov 2026 (some infobox figures came from a summary). See also Guha (2017).

overallCertainty.value: High for statistics and events. Kashmir and recent politics are contested, so this entry uses neutral wording.
